# secaudit

The Codex form of SecAudit's `/secaudit` command. It runs when the user names it (`$secaudit`), and
whatever they wrote after the name is its arguments.

## Reading this under Codex

The kit's skills and its verifier agent are written once, in Claude Code's vocabulary, and this
plugin carries them unchanged. Read them with this table:

| The text says | Under Codex |
| --- | --- |
| the **security-audit** skill | this plugin's `security-audit` skill (`secaudit:security-audit`). Open its `SKILL.md` and follow it, `references/` included. |
| `/secaudit`, any `/command` | the skill of the same name: `$secaudit`, `$secaudit-code`, `$secaudit-deps`, `$secaudit-passive`. |
| Read / Grep / Glob | shell read commands (`cat`, `sed -n`, `rg`, `ls`) |
| WebSearch / WebFetch | the web search tool |
| Task, "a background subagent" | spawn an agent and wait for its result |
| the `secaudit-verifier` agent | the custom agent of that name when this session has one; otherwise a default agent given the `developer_instructions` of [agents/secaudit-verifier.toml](../../agents/secaudit-verifier.toml) as its instructions. Either way it is read-only: it reports, it does not edit. |

Two things differ from Claude Code, and both matter:

1. **The command allowlist is a rule here, not a harness limit.** In Claude Code this command may
   run only the shell commands below without asking. Codex has no per-skill allowlist, so the
   same list binds as a rule: while this skill is running, ask the user before running anything
   outside it.

   `curl -sS`, `curl -I`, `command -v`, `dig`, `nslookup`, `semgrep`, `opengrep`, `osv-scanner`, `trivy fs`, `trivy config`, `trivy image`, `gitleaks detect`, `trufflehog filesystem`, `noseyparker`, `testssl.sh`, `sslscan`, `npm audit`, `npm audit signatures`, `pnpm audit`, `yarn npm audit`, `pip-audit`, `safety check`, `govulncheck`, `cargo audit`, `composer audit`, `bundle audit`, `dotnet list package`, `checkov`, `tfsec`, `kics`, `kube-score`, `kube-bench`, `zizmor`, `grype`, `syft`, `retire`

2. **The authorization hook runs only once it is trusted.** Codex skips a plugin's hook until the
   user has reviewed it in `/hooks`. Until then the passive-by-default posture rests on the
   skill's own authorization gate, which binds either way. A command that was not blocked is not
   a command that was authorized.

## Procedure

Run the **security-audit** skill against the target below.

Target / arguments: the arguments given with this skill — whatever the user wrote after `$secaudit`

Instructions:

1. If no target is given, use the current working directory as a **source target**.
2. Parse flags from the arguments:
   - `--lang tr|en` — report language (default: match the user's language, else English).
   - `--passive` — never send active/probe requests, even to a live target (recon only).
   - `--active` — the user is asserting authorization for active testing; still confirm
     ownership/scope per the skill's authorization gate before probing.
   - `--code` — treat the target as source code only (skip live requests).
   - `--deps` — limit to dependency + secret + SBOM scanning.
3. Follow the security-audit skill: detect target type and available tools, enforce the
   authorization gate, run the phased methodology (passive recon → attack surface →
   known CVEs/deps → OWASP web/API → source review → infra → mobile/LLM if applicable),
   verify findings with minimal safe proof, and produce the final report in the
   skill's report format.

Default posture is **safe/passive**. Never perform DoS, brute-force, data
exfiltration, or produce weaponized exploits. State that the result is a best-effort
assessment, not a guarantee.
